title: Water and dry air (curves against temperature)
licence: Correlations are published formulas; reference points are facts from the cited table; the compiled pack is released under the MIT licence of this repository
status: Computed curves from published correlations, checked against a reference table; suitable for hand calculations, see each property's rel_uncertainty

sources.ref: G. S. Kell, Density, thermal expansivity and compressibility of liquid water from 0 to 150 C, J. Chem. Eng. Data 20(1), 97-105 (1975)
Vogel-form viscosity fit mu = 2.414e-5 * 10^(247.8/(T-140)) Pa s; checked here against the IAPWS-based table at https://www.chem-casts.com/knowledge/viscosity-of-water
IAPWS R7-97(2012), Revised Release on the IAPWS Industrial Formulation 1997, section 8.1 saturation-pressure equation
Ideal-gas law with the specific gas constant of dry air, 287.05 J/(kg K)
F. M. White, Viscous Fluid Flow, Sutherland constants for air (viscosity: 1.716e-5 Pa s, 273.15 K, 110.4 K; conductivity: 0.0241 W/(m K), 273 K, 194 K)
Y. A. Cengel and J. M. Cimbala, Fluid Mechanics: Fundamentals and Applications, 3rd ed., McGraw-Hill (2014), Table A-3 (saturated water) and Table A-9 (air at 1 atm)
